events.title: JSON-RPC 1.0 published
events.summary: [JSON]-RPC.org published the [JSON]-RPC 1.0 specification in 2005 — a lightweight remote procedure call protocol using [JSON] over [HTTP].
events.about: [JSON]-RPC wraps method calls in [JSON] objects — `{"method":"subtract","params":[42,23],"id":1}` — and returns structured results or errors. Simpler than SOAP, it powered [Bitcoin] nodes, Ethereum clients, and countless internal APIs before gRPC and GraphQL. Example: a wallet app calls `getBalance` on a node with one POST and a typed [JSON] response.

narrative.whyChosen: [JSON]-RPC gave web-era developers a minimal RPC format without [XML] envelopes.
narrative.whyImportant: It influenced later specs (2.0, [JSON]-RPC over WebSocket) and [blockchain] node APIs.
narrative.problemSolved: [XML]-RPC and SOAP were heavy; AJAX-era apps needed thin RPC over [HTTP] with JavaScript-friendly payloads.
